open_questions: Mass still requires RV, but prior is low if variability
Individual sector light curves and spot modelling would confirm spot origin
dossier.public_summary: The dip appears on the target star and is flat-bottomed with no secondary, but its depth changes dramatically between transits and between sectors, with two deep outliers providing most of the signal over a star that shows large 1.4-day spot variations. Together this is best explained by stellar variability and noisy/few transits rather than a steady 3.1 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Depths scatter far more than expected; 2 of 6 transits are 2x-2.5x the mean and dominate the signal. Positive evidence for a few good bad transits/low SNR noise, not steady transits.
reasons.value: p_consistent=2.428659294109015e-18, top-3 share=0.972, outliers 566 ppm (1783) vs 10517 ppm (k=5.8 sigma)

reasons.why: Depth not constant between sectors; sector_depths_by_source also says changes_within_a_source with same low p_constant.

Star is strongly spotted/variable with large spin modulation and a ~11.1 d harmonic (7.96x rotation). Spots can mimic periodic dips and cause depth changes between sectors/transits, favouring variability over planet.
reasons.value: rotation 1.394 d, amplitude 11139-14299 ppm, phase_curve ratio_to_depth=0.06123 chi2=4.391

reasons.why: While individual checks are planet-like, the flat-bottom V and on-target centroid alone do not outweigh the large transit-to-transit and sector depth changes and high spot variability, which canonically produce flat-looking but unstable dips.
reasons.value: rp_rearth=3.135, shape v_sigma=-2.889, centroid offset_sigma=1.501 on_target, secondary snr=2.586

reasons.why: Independent scorer ranks this well below the median planet (0.5) and in the bottom 10% where false positives dominate, consistent with the outliers/variability evidence.
